author: agent-1
purpose: Close ARCH.RETENTION-TIERS after both reviewers rejected excerpt-T1 as the universal default. Keep the tiered/declared ladder (that part was right). Redefine T1 so durable explainability answers why for local, path-relationship, and negative-absence findings without defaulting to a source archive (T2).

decisionDependencies.claim: excerpt-T1 is lint-shaped and cannot prove cycles, blast radius, or dead code
mutable current tier conflicts with immutable Run
graph/blast-radius/dead-code are the product wedge, not an edge case

problem.wrongInsight: Explaining a finding requires the spans it cited.
problem.whyWrong: True for local predicates. False as a general theory: path findings need edge sets; negative findings need closed-world Coverage of a relation. The product's differentiated value is relationship analysis (04).
whatSurvives: Explainability is tiered and declared per Run, not absolute
RT-1 manifest field; RT-3 forward-only config; RT-4 inventory; RT-5 fail-loud for insufficient tier
T2 is read-set-bounded full replay, not whole-repo archive
Privacy classes apply at every tier

findingShapes.proofObject: subject span(s) + optional local AST/context excerpt
ordered path certificate or SCC member list: edge ids with endpoint symbol/file identities; optional hop display spans
subject identity + Coverage certificate for the reference (or relevant) relation over declared scope/partition roots — proof of exhaustive absence, not a positive cite
findingShapes.display: subject location excerpt only (display, not proof)

tiers.answers: what was concluded; which inputs by identity; whether required Coverage held
tiers.cannotAnswer: why, in proof terms, for any finding shape

retains: for each finding: the sealed FindingProof object (see proofSchema)
optional display excerpts referenced by the proof (privacy-classed, bounded)
tiers.answers: why this finding for all three finding shapes, without retaining the full read-set
tiers.cannotAnswer: byte-identical re-derivation of all facts; attestation-grade replay
tiers.size: small-to-medium; bounded by proof budgets (see bounds)
tiers.whyDefault: T0 cannot answer why. T2 retains all read-set bytes (source archive of everything the analysis touched). T1-proof is the minimum that satisfies the product's explainability promise for the wedge capabilities while remaining minimising relative to T2.

retains: all read-set bytes required to re-derive under the same Plan/toolchain identities
tiers.size: large; read-set bounded not repository bounded

proofSchema.rule: Every finding at T1+ carries exactly one sealed proof whose kind matches the rule's declared findingShape.

kinds.edges: ordered list of edge identities (from, to, relation, evidence digests)
kinds.note: SCC findings may use memberSet + cycleWitness path instead of a single path
coverageDigest commits to the closed-world claim; without it the finding is not explainable at T1

proofSchema.rulesDeclareShape: Each rule/profile declares findingShape ∈ {local, path, absence, composite}. Composite findings carry a list of sub-proofs.
proofSchema.noProofNoSeal: A Run cannot seal at T1 if any finding lacks a well-typed FindingProof.

t0FactBodies.statement: T0 does NOT pin full fact relation bodies by default. T0 pins digests of fact partitions and Coverage. Full fact bodies needed for path/absence proofs are either (a) embedded or referenced inside FindingProof at T1, or (b) retained only if the project opts into a T1 variant that pins declared relation partitions (T1-partition) — see optionalVariants.
t0FactBodies.why: If T0 silently kept all facts, T1 would be UX-only and size claims would be false. If T0 keeps only digests, relationship why cannot live at T0.

optionalVariants.meaning: T1-proof plus pinned fact-partition bodies for relations named by the Plan's required Coverage
optionalVariants.when: agent workflows that re-query the same Run's graph without T2
optionalVariants.privacyNote: Larger; must appear in inventory with size

immutability.sealedTier: Immutable field of the sealed Run manifest. Never rewritten.
immutability.retentionState: NOT a second mutable tier field on the Run. The store tracks which proof/bytes objects remain reachable (GC/retention state). Projections may report effectiveExplainability ∈ {full-at-sealed-tier, degraded, unavailable} derived from reachability, without mutating the sealed manifest.
immutability.degradation: One-way loss of reachable objects. Reporting is honest: if FindingProof bytes were GC'd, effectiveExplainability becomes degraded/unavailable even though sealedTier remains T1-proof.
immutability.rejects: RT-2 as previously written if it meant rewriting currentTier on the sealed Run. Replace RT-2 with sealedTier + effectiveExplainability projection.

requirements.requirement: sealedTier is a field of the sealed Run manifest, never ambient-only configuration
Sealed tier is immutable; effective explainability is a projection of object reachability and may degrade one-way; never silently claim sealed power after GC
Every tier and FindingProof is privacy-classed and appears in data inventory with size
requirements.status: retained and strengthened for proof objects

requirements.requirement: Policy requiring T2 or T1-proof fails loud against insufficient effective explainability
requirements.status: retained; check effective, not only sealed

requirements.requirement: Default sealedTier is T1-proof; rules that cannot emit FindingProof cannot ship as default-gate rules
Proof budgets: max edges per path proof, max members per SCC witness, max excerpt bytes per finding — exhaustion is Coverage/diagnostic, not silent truncation of proof

bounds.sccWitnessMaxMembers: default proposal 32 with digest of full member set if truncated
bounds.onBudgetExhaustion: FindingProof records truncation=true and residualDigest; consumer must not treat truncated proof as complete path

defaultAndDisclosure.firstRun: Disclose sealedTier, what T1-proof retains (proof objects may include identifiers and bounded excerpts), storage location (TM V2), how to choose T0 or T2
interactionWithTM: V10 residual must stop advertising T1-excerpt as default

V4 excerpt-off-by-default applies to display materialisation into reports/export; FindingProof may still retain bounded display excerpts at T1 under privacy class — materialisation to support bundles remains explicit
R4 source bytes only when required: T1-proof is not full source; T2 is

conformanceTests.assert: A cycle finding sealed at T1-proof carries a path or SCC witness; a golden with only a package-name span fails.
A dead-code finding at T1-proof carries absence proof (coverageDigest + relation + scope roots); subject excerpt alone fails.
A local lint finding at T1-proof may use kind=local with subjectAnchors only.
Two Runs with identical EvidenceDigest must have identical sealedTier; effectiveExplainability may differ only if object reachability differs and is reported.
GC that deletes FindingProof objects cannot leave sealedTier claiming T1 while effectiveExplainability reports full.
Attestation policy requiring T2 rejects a T1-proof Run loudly.
Path proof exceeding pathMaxEdges sets truncation=true and does not silently drop edges without residualDigest.
